conclusion: Two different numbers, both correct, explained by parameter tying. (1) The five shards store 5174964736 parameters = 5.1750 B. (2) After loading, summing every parameter NAME without de-duplication gives the identical 5174964736 = 5.1750 B, so the checkpoint and the model hold exactly the same named tensors: 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 dropped. (3) Summing UNIQUE parameter objects gives 4539265536 = 4.5393 B, which is the figure round 1 quoted. The gap is 635699200 = 0.6357 B and equals vocab_size*hidden_size = 635699200 exactly. Evidence that this is tying rather than loss: (a) config.json declares tie_word_embeddings=true; (b) the checkpoint contains BOTH lm_head.weight and model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight with identical shape [248320, 2560]; (c) loading reports 0 missing / 0 unexpected / 0 mismatched keys; (d) at runtime both names resolve to the SAME Parameter object (identical data_ptr), observed with named_parameters(remove_duplicate=False). Therefore the 0.6357 B is one shared matrix counted twice in the shard arithmetic, not weights that went missing.
